meaning:
κατ-αισχύνω
[in LXX chiefly for בּוּשׁ ;]
to disgrace, dishonour, put to shame: with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.11:4-5; with accusative of person(s), 1Co.1:27 11:22; pass., to be ashamed: Luk.13:17, 2Co.7:14 9:4, 1Pe.3:16; as in LXX (Psa.22:6 25:2-3, al.), of unfulfilled hopes: Rom.5:5; pass., Rom.9:33 10:11, 1Pe.2:6" (LXX) .†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: will never be put to shame
will never be put to shame

elsewhere.note: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
but God chose the foolish things of the world that he might put to shame those who are wise. God chose the weak things of the world that he might put to shame…
For if in anything I have boasted to him on your behalf, I was not disappointed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made…
Because it is contained in Scripture, “Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious: He who believes in him will not be disappointed.”
